chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no believer who washes a believer and says while washing him, 'Lord, Your forgiveness, Your forgiveness,' except that Allah forgives him.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for washing a deceased believer?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing that the act of washing a fellow believer is not merely a physical duty but a means of securing personal divine pardon through the specific supplication 'Rabb 'afwaka 'afwaka' (My Lord, Your forgiveness, Your forgiveness). This highlights the Shia emphasis on communal solidarity (ta'awun) and the spiritual efficacy of mindful intention (niyyah) during funeral rites, linking the washer's spiritual state directly to the deceased's honor.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is none from a Believer who washes a Believer and is saying while washing him, ‘Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Your Forgiveness, Your<sup>azwj</sup> Forgiveness (for him)’, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Forgive him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Any believing person who when washing the dead body of a believing person says, “O Allah grant him forgiveness,” Allah then grants forgiveness to him also.’”
